# Fusion Airfoil Plugin

## Installation

1. Download the [Airfoil DAT Importer Fusion Add-in .zip file](./assets/Fusion Airfoil DAT importer.zip)[^1].  
2. Locate the downloaded .zip file with Finder. It will likely be in your *Downloads* folder.  
   ![][image1]  
3. Double-click the .zip file. It will unpack the contents to a new folder.  
   ![][image2]  
4. Start a new design in Fusion.  
5. Click *UTILITIES*, then *Scripts and Add Ins*.  
   ![][image3]  
6. Click *\+*, then *Script or add-in from device*.  
   ![][image4]  
7. **Single-click** the folder that was created in step 3 to select it.  
   **IMPORTANT:** Do not double click the folder and select any files inside it. The folder itself must be selected\!  
   ![][image5]  
8. Click *Open*.  
9. Find the name *RC CAD Airfoil Dat Importer* in the list. Turn the *Run* toggle switch ON, and check the *Run on Startup* box as shown below.  
   ![][image6]

## Usage

### Import the Airfoil Data

10. Turn on the *Origin* view.  
   ![][image7]  
11. Select *Import Airfoil* from the *Create* menu.  
     
   *Note: if you don’t see this menu item, complete the Install Plug-in section of this guide first.*  
     
   ![][image8]  
3. Import the airfoil data:  
   1. Click *Browse…* and select the .dat file you downloaded.  
   2. Choose a Chord Length. Something in the range of about 30-60 mm is about right for the size we will build, but this is your option.  
   3. Select one of the Origin planes in your design to create a new sketch on.  
   4. Click *OK*.

   ![][image9]

A new sketch is created in your design with points from the airfoil data file.

4. Locate and edit the new sketch. You might need to click the \> to expand the *Sketches* category.  
   ![][image10]

### Option: No Taper

Simply extrude the profile to the blade length you want.

![][image11]

### Option: Tapered

1. Select the *Offset Plane* tool.  
   ![][image12]  
2. Select the same plane on the origin that the first sketch was drawn on.  
   ![][image13]  
3. Drag the plane to your desired blade length.  
   ![][image14]  
4. Repeat the earlier steps to import airfoil data:  
   1. Creating the new sketch on the offset plane  
   2. Choose a smaller chord length  
   3. Edit the new sketch to close the shape as required

You should now have two sketches with different sizes of airfoil shapes.  
![][image15]

5. Select the *Loft* tool.  
   ![][image16]  
6. Click to select the first airfoil profile, then the second. The loft tool will **interpolate** between them.  
   ![][image17]  
   Because the second profile had a different chord length than the first, the final object will be tapered as seen from above, reducing the mass of the blade from root to tip.  
   ![][image18]

### Option: Blended Airfoil Profiles

You can use more than one airfoil design. Repeat the above steps, but use a different airfoil profile for the second sketch. The *Loft* tool will blend them.

### Option: Twist

You can gradually twist the airfoil from root to tip to better adjust for the slower airspeed near the root to the faster airspeed near the tip.

* Repeat the above steps, creating multiple offset planes along the length of the blade.  
* Rotate each sketch profile around a point that is approximately 25% from the front of the blade.  
* Select all the profiles for the *Loft* tool.

![][image19]


[^1]:  Source: [RC CAD LLC](https://www.rccad2vr.com/howto/install-fusion-360-script-airfoils-dat)
